coreBackstory: Bert has worked this land for forty years — his father before him, and his grandfather before that.
greetings: Mornin'. You here about the grain, or you just lost?
Don't just stand there gawkin'. Come in or go on, but don't block the door.
Ah, a face I recognize. You want bread, or you want business?
idleChatter: The land's been restless. Plants don't lie — somethin' ain't right.
My granddad used to say: 'When the mill whispers, the earth is listening.' I thought it was just stories.
Rain's comin'. Can smell it in the air. Three days, maybe four.
Young folks these days don't know good soil if they're standin' in it.
farewells: Take some bread for the road. You look like you haven't eaten proper in days.
Don't go wanderin' the fields after dark. Not safe, and I ain't just talkin' about pests.
Come back when the harvest's in. I'll have fresh cider worth celebratin'.
reactiveComments: You've got the look of someone who's seen things. The land's got that effect.
If you're headed to the old ruins, stay clear of the eastern field. Ground's unstable there.
Strange folk been passin' through. Hooded types. Didn't like the look of 'em.
